svg.text: E from K and G (P5668, P5673)
Each mark is a material on Wikidata (filled circles: Young's modulus as recorded; triangles: E = 9KG/(3K+G) from the bulk and shear moduli, mostly elements and minerals). The
dashed lines pass through steel: a material on a line gives a part of the same stiffness at the same mass as steel; above and to the left of it, lighter. Read the three lines: on the
slope-1 line (ties, E/ρ) steel, aluminium and titanium sit together; on the slope-3 line (panels, E^⅓/ρ) aluminium, magnesium, beryllium, carbon-fibre polyamide and above all
spruce are far above steel. Hover a material for its indices and rank; click it to open it on Wikidata. Caveat: a crowd-curated sample (about 30 engineering materials, a few
hundred computed-looking element and mineral values without references).
